source.title: Source context for eleven final principal-route length conventions

source_locators: Sprintall et al.2009 introduction paragraphs3-8: western Sulawesi/Makassar inflow and Lombok/Ombai/Timor exits. Tables1-2 are2004-2006 transport context; passage widths are not route lengths. Retained conceptual passage network remains unmodified.

Comas-Rodriguez2011 introduction/section3.2: subsurface westward AzCC north of AzC; local section24.5W,35.25-36.25N. Retained alongflow review explicitly finds no established zonally continuous surface route. Broader model counterflow context: Onken1993 and Volkov/Fu2010 DOI10.1175/2010JPO4326.1.

Bower et al.2000 Part2 regional pathways: Hormuz/Gulf of Oman descent, northern cascade near25deg20N57E and rejoining near24deg50N56deg50E, then Oman-margin spreading. Downstream handoff toward Ras al Hadd is an OSW reference convention.

Melet et al.2010 abstract and sections1/3.1 printed1302-1303/1307-1308: Coral Sea inflow, coastal NGCU to Vitiaz, then north PNG toward equatorial connection. Ueki2003 DOI10.1029/2002JC001611 supplies separate142E mooring support; no complete axis extracted.

Melet et al.2010 abstract/section3.1 printed1308: NBCU/SICU/SEC feed NICU along New Ireland to its tip near2S, where it splits westward and retroflects toward EUC. Original text reviewed; no modeled axis digitized.

Melet et al.2010 abstract/section3.1: modeled SICU formed where SEC meets eastern Solomon Islands, follows eastern flank and joins NICU feeding. Original source describes proposal and limited observational support.

de Pascual-Collar et al.2019 introduction: Gibraltar overflow descends across Gulf of Cadiz, rounds Cape St Vincent, enters Tagus Basin reservoir then branches. Bower2002 DOI10.1029/2001JC001007 describes local lower-core AMUSE reach; not a full axis.

Dengler et al.2004 introduction: NADW carried from Greenland/Scotland and Labrador Sea toward South Atlantic and ACC; breakup into eddies near8S. Existing47N-24.5N study reach from OS2023 DOI10.5194/os-19-1009-2023 is retained separately.
Chapter6 printed70 / PDF80, March2005 version: polar easterlies drive westward narrow coastal East Wind Drift, distinct from eastward ACC.
Chapter8 Figure8.6 printed111 and printed125-126: surface New Guinea Coastal Current in April-November trade-wind phase, reversing December-March. Separate persistent deeper flow excluded.

Peters et al.2005 PartI sections1-3 and Figure1 printed571: Bab el Mandeb to northern descending channel and Tadjoura Rift equilibration, two preferred channels.130km channel description differs from source-to-handoff route. Original Figure1 reviewed.

source.scope_caution: These are declared approximate principal reference extents. They do not establish current continuity, passage axes, plume boundaries, canonical aliases, or physical measurement admission.

method: WGS84 geodesic leg sums through explicit geographic reference extents. Source text/maps identify named-flow geography; OSW chooses the handoffs and connecting controls.

sensitivity.interpretation: Route-specific endpoint/drawing sensitivity. Coastal entries can declare smaller or one-sided offshore offsets. These are not physical confidence limits or annual variation; all cases retained.

dateline_policy: Shortest geodesics; continuous display unwrapping and periodic coarse land copies.

currents.source_locator: Chapter6 printed70 / PDF80, March2005 version: polar easterlies drive westward narrow coastal East Wind Drift, distinct from eastward ACC.
currents.scope: Idealized one-circuit coastal-envelope convention around Antarctica in westward orientation, with the0E seam closed once. Islands, gyre loops, ice-shelf cavity circulation and offshore ACC are excluded. Gaps between coastal regimes are conceptual reference connections, not evidence of an uninterrupted circumpolar fluid jet.
currents.source_time_convention: Undated geographic system reference. Ice-front positions and actual occupied coastal branches vary; no monthly axis or annual length range inferred.
currents.identity_interpretation: A closed geographic reference circuit for the catalogued East Wind Drift system, not a measured coastline, Antarctic Slope Current alias, or proven continuous current.
currents.gate_rationale: Rounded OSW principal-route handoffs and connecting controls. Source geography motivates the convention, but does not supply a complete observed axis. Conditional route/continuity assumptions remain explicit. Revised Peninsula/Victoria Land bends avoid interpolating through the continent; no current or ice-front digitization is implied.

currents.source_locator: Comas-Rodriguez2011 introduction/section3.2: subsurface westward AzCC north of AzC; local section24.5W,35.25-36.25N. Retained alongflow review explicitly finds no established zonally continuous surface route. Broader model counterflow context: Onken1993 and Volkov/Fu2010 DOI10.1175/2010JPO4326.1.
currents.scope: Conditional subsurface return-envelope convention from eastern Azores-system handoff17W36N westward to an assumed western recirculation handoff40W36.5N. Not a concatenation of surface drift signals or transverse sections. AzC eastward jet and plateau recirculation loops excluded.
currents.source_time_convention: Geographic subsurface hypothesis informed by different studies; not an October2009 axis, year-round surface route or measured monthly climatology.
currents.identity_interpretation: Full endpoints/continuity unresolved.17W and40W are explicit OSW assumed system handoffs. The110km survey span is width and is not used as length.
currents.gate_rationale: Rounded OSW principal-route handoffs and connecting controls. Source geography motivates the convention, but does not supply a complete observed axis. Conditional route/continuity assumptions remain explicit.

currents.source_locator: Dengler et al.2004 introduction: NADW carried from Greenland/Scotland and Labrador Sea toward South Atlantic and ACC; breakup into eddies near8S. Existing47N-24.5N study reach from OS2023 DOI10.5194/os-19-1009-2023 is retained separately.
currents.scope: Atlantic boundary-following principal geographic corridor from Labrador outflow handoff58N54W to southern-Atlantic/ACC exchange handoff45S48W. Deep eddy-mediated and discontinuous portions are conceptual corridor connections. Excludes upstream formation-basin loops, interior alternatives, full AMOC return path and subsequent ACC flow.
currents.source_time_convention: Undated circulation corridor synthesis, not an observed continuous particle itinerary or a single deep density-layer axis.
currents.identity_interpretation: Boundary continuity is not proven: the source explicitly documents breakup near8S. This number is the declared corridor length, not a claim of one continuous deep jet.
currents.gate_rationale: Rounded OSW principal-route handoffs and connecting controls. Source geography motivates the convention, but does not supply a complete observed axis. Conditional route/continuity assumptions remain explicit. Northeast Brazil controls explicitly bend around Cape Sao Roque and the offshore margin instead of interpolating across land.

currents.source_locator: Sprintall et al.2009 introduction paragraphs3-8: western Sulawesi/Makassar inflow and Lombok/Ombai/Timor exits. Tables1-2 are2004-2006 transport context; passage widths are not route lengths. Retained conceptual passage network remains unmodified.
currents.scope: Selected western upper-thermocline principal passage route: Pacific/Sulawesi entry, Makassar, western Flores Sea, Lombok exit to Indian Ocean. Other inflows, Banda detours, Ombai/Timor exits and recirculations are not added. This is one complete declared inflow-to-outflow itinerary, not the sum or full geographic length of the network.
currents.source_time_convention: Geographic principal-route convention;2004-2006 source transport means do not provide a dated axis or permanent one-way flow at all depths.
currents.identity_interpretation: Passage network requires a selected itinerary. Lombok is the explicit exit convention here; no unique network-wide physical current length or fixed slab is claimed.
currents.gate_rationale: Rounded OSW principal-route handoffs and connecting controls. Source geography motivates the convention, but does not supply a complete observed axis. Conditional route/continuity assumptions remain explicit.

currents.source_locator: de Pascual-Collar et al.2019 introduction: Gibraltar overflow descends across Gulf of Cadiz, rounds Cape St Vincent, enters Tagus Basin reservoir then branches. Bower2002 DOI10.1029/2001JC001007 describes local lower-core AMUSE reach; not a full axis.
currents.scope: Declared boundary-undercurrent principal route from western Gibraltar outlet to Tagus Basin reservoir handoff near38.5N. Includes Gulf of Cadiz descent and Cape St Vincent turn. Excludes meddy loops, far-field water-mass tongues, poleward European spreading and African branches.
currents.source_time_convention: Geographic lower-core/boundary-current convention informed by studies with different years; no single-depth dated axis or annual extrema.
currents.identity_interpretation: Handoff into the reservoir defines the reference end; distant Mediterranean Water salinity is not treated as continuation of the named undercurrent.
currents.gate_rationale: Rounded OSW principal-route handoffs and connecting controls. Source geography motivates the convention, but does not supply a complete observed axis. Conditional route/continuity assumptions remain explicit. Gibraltar outlet alternatives vary longitude; moving the initial alternative north had placed six scenarios on coarse Spanish land.

currents.source_locator: Chapter8 Figure8.6 printed111 and printed125-126: surface New Guinea Coastal Current in April-November trade-wind phase, reversing December-March. Separate persistent deeper flow excluded.
currents.scope: Declared north-New-Guinea surface envelope from downstream Vitiaz approach147E to western coastal/retroflection handoff134E0.5N. Excludes Vitiaz inflow passage, Halmahera eddy loops and thermocline NGCU.
currents.source_time_convention: April-November northwestward trade-wind convention; surface flow reverses in northwest monsoon. Not a dated monthly axis.
currents.identity_interpretation: Western handoff and connections beyond the existing146E-142E study reach are editorial geographic estimates, not new observed continuity.
currents.gate_rationale: Rounded OSW principal-route handoffs and connecting controls. Source geography motivates the convention, but does not supply a complete observed axis. Conditional route/continuity assumptions remain explicit.

currents.source_locator: Melet et al.2010 abstract and sections1/3.1 printed1302-1303/1307-1308: Coral Sea inflow, coastal NGCU to Vitiaz, then north PNG toward equatorial connection. Ueki2003 DOI10.1029/2002JC001611 supplies separate142E mooring support; no complete axis extracted.
currents.scope: Selected NGCU principal thermocline route from southern Solomon/PNG feed near153E10.5S via coastal approach and Vitiaz to western equatorial handoff136E. Excludes North Queensland upstream, New Britain branch, NICU branch and downstream EUC.
currents.source_time_convention: Undated principal geographic itinerary; source modeled seasonality and local mooring years are not a uniform observed layer or dated axis.
currents.identity_interpretation: Vitiaz and cross-equatorial connection extend the prior north-PNG regional reach under an explicit principal-route convention. Other thermocline branches are not summed.
currents.gate_rationale: Rounded OSW principal-route handoffs and connecting controls. Source geography motivates the convention, but does not supply a complete observed axis. Conditional route/continuity assumptions remain explicit.

currents.source_locator: Melet et al.2010 abstract/section3.1 printed1308: NBCU/SICU/SEC feed NICU along New Ireland to its tip near2S, where it splits westward and retroflects toward EUC. Original text reviewed; no modeled axis digitized.
currents.scope: Selected NICU principal route from Solomon-side source confluence154E5S along east New Ireland, past northern tip, to equatorial eastward-retroflection handoff152E0. Excludes separate NBCU/SICU source lengths, westward Bismarck branch and downstream EUC.
currents.source_time_convention: Undated geographic itinerary; June-August stronger modeled connection is source context, not a dated or all-season axis.
currents.identity_interpretation: Explicitly selects the EUC-feeding branch at the northern split; the alternative westward branch is not added.
currents.gate_rationale: Rounded OSW principal-route handoffs and connecting controls. Source geography motivates the convention, but does not supply a complete observed axis. Conditional route/continuity assumptions remain explicit.

currents.source_locator: Melet et al.2010 abstract/section3.1: modeled SICU formed where SEC meets eastern Solomon Islands, follows eastern flank and joins NICU feeding. Original source describes proposal and limited observational support.
currents.scope: Conditional whole eastern-island-chain SICU reference envelope from southern offshore SEC/island confluence164E11S to northern NICU-feeding handoff155E3.5S. Excludes SEC basin reach, Solomon Strait passage, NICU length and EUC.
currents.source_time_convention: Modeled mean geographic interpretation; not a new observational admission, fixed annual axis or continuous measured coastal jet.
currents.identity_interpretation: SICU is retained with the source proposal/model qualification. The reference connector does not resolve observational continuity.
currents.gate_rationale: Rounded OSW principal-route handoffs and connecting controls. Source geography motivates the convention, but does not supply a complete observed axis. Conditional route/continuity assumptions remain explicit.

currents.source_locator: Bower et al.2000 Part2 regional pathways: Hormuz/Gulf of Oman descent, northern cascade near25deg20N57E and rejoining near24deg50N56deg50E, then Oman-margin spreading. Downstream handoff toward Ras al Hadd is an OSW reference convention.
currents.scope: Selected northern cascading plume/boundary route from Hormuz outlet to Oman-margin/Ras al Hadd handoff into Arabian Sea intermediate-water spreading. Southern branch, eddy detours, other Gulf source-water paths and far-field salinity tongue excluded.
currents.source_time_convention: Undated principal descending-plume and margin-spreading convention; not one observed trajectory or annual plume boundary.
currents.identity_interpretation: Reference endpoint is the boundary-to-open-Arabian-Sea handoff, not the furthest detectable Persian Gulf Water. Exact plume equilibration and branch continuity vary.
currents.gate_rationale: Rounded OSW principal-route handoffs and connecting controls. Source geography motivates the convention, but does not supply a complete observed axis. Conditional route/continuity assumptions remain explicit. Seaward Ras al Hamra bend preserves the Oman-margin route without drawing over the headland.
currents.fixed_drawing_vertex_rationale: East-Musandam offshore passage control prevents latitude probes from cutting the headland. All other vertices/endpoints and all36 cases retained.

currents.scope: Selected northern-plume principal route from Bab el Mandeb outlet through Northern Channel to Tadjoura Rift equilibration/turning handoff. Excludes Southern Channel length, deep-rift recirculation and far-field Red Sea Water spreading through Gulf of Aden.
currents.source_time_convention: Geographic principal-plume convention. Winter and summer REDSOX2001 differ in strength/equilibration; this is not either dated axis or an annual length range.
currents.identity_interpretation: One complete declared descending-plume itinerary, not the sum of both channels or the entire far-field salinity distribution.
